title: The Feud Over the Fig Tree

collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS - LIVING CULTURE V: FAMILY DRAMA, FEUDS AND LEADERSHIP DISPUTES (LCE-01..50, draft, 2026-11-18)
All sorts of real-life drama suited to Isola: parents with opinions about who their children marry, arranged matches, inheritances, feuds between families, accusations, apologies that are not enough, and arguments about who should lead.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. The owner waived the review ("I'm sure the draft events are fine"); every event passed the Isola rules and the final 15-point review, logged in the notes.

collection.description: Two families have feuded for years over who owns a fig tree: split the figs, or ask the elders to judge.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: The fig tree between (subject)'s hut and (friend)'s hut has been the subject of a feud for three generations. Each family says their great-grandparent planted it. This season the tree is heavy with figs, and both families are standing under it with baskets, glaring. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: (subject) suggests splitting the figs, half each, without deciding who owns the tree. (friend) agrees, suspiciously. They pick together in silence. Halfway through, (friend) passes (subject) a basket without being asked. The feud is not over. But it has slowed down.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: The elders hear the whole history: three generations of stories. They decide the tree belongs to the village and anyone may pick from it. Both families are furious. The feud now has a new target: the elders.
